workflow.critical: The workflow execution engine is governed by: {project-root}/_bmad/core/tasks/workflow.xml
You MUST have already loaded and processed: {installed_path}/workflow.yaml
Communicate all responses in {communication_language} and generate all documents in {document_output_language}
WORKTREE SUPPORT: {project-root} = current working directory (pwd). NEVER use 'cd' to navigate elsewhere. All paths are relative to cwd.

context-boundaries.available: Injected context with feature_description, input_files (docs), run metadata; codebase for discovery; git history
context-boundaries.focus: Creating comprehensive, implementation-ready plans with exhaustive developer guidance
context-boundaries.limits: Do not implement the feature; do not skip artifact analysis; output pure markdown to stdout
context-boundaries.dependencies: Context must include feature_description; input_files optional but recommended

workflow.critical: 🔥 CRITICAL MISSION: You are creating the ULTIMATE story context engine that prevents LLM developer mistakes, omissions or disasters! 🔥
Your purpose is NOT to copy from epics - it's to create a comprehensive, optimized story file that gives the DEV agent EVERYTHING needed for flawless implementation

COMMON LLM MISTAKES TO PREVENT: reinventing wheels, wrong libraries, wrong file locations, breaking regressions, ignoring UX, vague implementations, lying about completion, not learning from past work
🚨 EXHAUSTIVE ANALYSIS REQUIRED: You must thoroughly analyze ALL artifacts to extract critical context - do NOT be lazy or skim! This is the most important function in the entire development process!
🔬 UTILIZE SUBPROCESSES AND SUBAGENTS: Use research subagents, subprocesses or parallel processing if available to thoroughly analyze different artifacts simultaneously and thoroughly
❓ SAVE QUESTIONS: If you think of questions or clarifications during analysis, save them for the end after the complete story is written
🎯 ZERO USER INTERVENTION: Process should be fully automated except for initial epic/story selection or missing documents

step.goal: Parse context and load input files
step.critical: Parse the full injected context object
step.action: Extract {{feature_description}} from context - this is the user's request
Extract {{input_files}} list from context - paths to documents to analyze
Extract {{platform}} from context if available (cli, web, mobile, backend)
Extract any other available context fields (artifacts, phase_history, etc.)

check.action: For each file path in {{input_files}}: - Read the file content - Categorize by type (architecture, PRD, requirements, design, etc.) based on filename/content - Store content for analysis in subsequent steps
check.note: Files may include: architecture docs, PRD, requirements, design specs, existing code references
No input files provided - will rely on codebase discovery and feature_description analysis

step.critical: Search codebase for existing patterns BEFORE creating new implementations - prevents reinventing wheels!
step.action: Extract keywords from {{feature_description}} to guide codebase search

Search codebase for existing implementations related to the feature: - Similar functionality that can be extended - Patterns and conventions already in use - Related modules or components - Existing utilities or helpers

check.note: These existing patterns will inform the implementation guidance

check.action: Get last 10 commit titles to understand recent work patterns

Analyze recent commits for relevance to the feature: - Files created/modified - Code patterns and conventions used - Library dependencies added/changed - Architecture decisions implemented - Testing approaches used

step.goal: Analyze input documents and feature requirements
step.critical: 🔬 EXHAUSTIVE ARTIFACT ANALYSIS - This is where you prevent future developer fuckups!
step.action: For each document loaded from {{input_files}}, extract relevant information:

check.if: requirements or PRD documents were loaded
check.action: Extract from requirements/PRD: - Business objectives and user value - Functional requirements related to {{feature_description}} - Non-functional requirements (performance, security, etc.) - Acceptance criteria if specified - User stories or use cases

Extract from architecture docs: - Technical stack: languages, frameworks, libraries with versions - Code structure: folder organization, naming conventions - API patterns: service structure, endpoint patterns - Database schemas if relevant - Security requirements and patterns - Testing standards and frameworks

check.if: design or UX documents were loaded
check.action: Extract from design docs: - User experience requirements - UI component specifications - Interaction patterns - Accessibility requirements
Perform deep analysis of {{feature_description}}: - Identify implied requirements - Determine likely technical approach - Note assumptions that need validation

step.goal: Web research for latest technical specifics

workflow.step:
🌐 ENSURE LATEST TECH KNOWLEDGE - Prevent outdated implementations! **WEB INTELLIGENCE:** Identify specific technical areas that require latest version knowledge:
From architecture analysis, identify specific libraries, APIs, or frameworks For each critical technology, research latest stable version and key changes: - Latest API documentation and breaking changes - Security vulnerabilities or updates - Performance improvements or deprecations - Best practices for current version
**EXTERNAL CONTEXT INCLUSION:** Include in story any critical latest information the developer needs: - Specific library versions and why chosen - API endpoints with parameters and authentication - Recent security patches or considerations - Performance optimization techniques - Migration considerations if upgrading

📝 CREATE ULTIMATE STORY FILE - The developer's master implementation guide!
Initialize from template.md: {default_output_file} story_header
story_requirements
conditional_docs_section Include {{conditional_docs_content}} in the story under "## Relevant Feature Documentation" section This gives the dev agent access to existing patterns and knowledge that matched this story's context
developer_context_section **DEV AGENT GUARDRAILS:** technical_requirements architecture_compliance library_framework_requirements
file_structure_requirements testing_requirements
previous_story_intelligence
git_intelligence_summary
latest_tech_information
project_context_reference
story_completion_status
Set story Status to: "ready-for-dev" Add completion note: "Ultimate context engine analysis completed - comprehensive developer guide created"

step.goal: Update sprint status, Linear integration, and finalize
step.action: Output the complete story/plan content to stdout as pure markdown
step.critical: The final LLM message MUST be the story content only - no wrapper, no status messages

success.item: Story file created at {story_dir}/{{story_key}}.md with all required sections
Exhaustive artifact analysis completed (epics, architecture, previous stories, git history)
Linear issue created OR updated to Todo status (if .linear config exists)
ADW state updated with story_id and plan_file (if ADW environment)

failure.item: No epic/story found in source files or sprint status
Incomplete or superficial artifact analysis (skimming instead of exhaustive review)
Missing critical developer context (architecture constraints, previous learnings)
Story file created without required sections or with placeholder content
Sprint status not updated after story creation
Linear integration failed without graceful fallback messaging
Proceeding without user input when story selection is ambiguous

workflow.master-rule: Skipping artifact analysis, optimizing sequences, or creating superficial story context is FORBIDDEN and constitutes SYSTEM FAILURE.
